ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal cavity

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and nasal cavity symptoms with a mass lesion
salient_findings: Nasal mass at the level of the left middle turbinate
Expansile, mildly enhancing soft-tissue mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity
key_facts: 4-month history of symptoms
Left eye proptosis
Diplopia
Chemosis
No epistaxis, headache, or nasal obstruction
Mass at the level of the left middle turbinate
Erosion of the upper nasal septum
Mild left proptosis with full extraocular movements
No papilledema
Normal visual acuity
Expansile, mildly enhancing soft-tissue mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity
Remodeling of the left medial orbital wall
Extension to the level of the cribriform plate
Retention of secretions in the left frontal sinus
No dural enhancement or intracranial extension on MRI
No intratumoral hemorrhage or cystic change on MRI

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal cavity

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity with orbital involvement

shortlist.label: Inverted papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile, mildly enhancing soft-tissue mass in the nasal cavity

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal cavity
shortlist.why_kept: Destructive mass in the nasal cavity with erosion of the upper nasal septum

shortlist.label: Olfactory neuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the nasal cavity with extension to the cribriform plate

shortlist.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive mass in the nasal cavity with destruction of the anterior skull base

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity, erosion of the upper nasal septum, and extension to the level of the cribriform plate, along with the absence of dural enhancement or intracranial extension on MRI, is consistent with esthesioneuroblastoma, a rare malignant tumor that originates from the olfactory epithelium.

rejected.label: Inverted papilloma
rejected.why: Inverted papilloma is typically a benign tumor and less likely to cause such extensive destruction and erosion of surrounding structures.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal cavity
rejected.why: Squamous cell carcinoma is more commonly associated with a history of tobacco use and would likely present with more aggressive features such as epistaxis, headache, or nasal obstruction, which are absent in this case.

rejected.label: Olfactory neuroblastoma
rejected.why: Olfactory neuroblastoma is another term for esthesioneuroblastoma, so it is essentially the same diagnosis as the chosen champion.

rejected.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
rejected.why: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma is a highly aggressive tumor that would likely present with more rapid progression of symptoms and more extensive invasion of surrounding structures, which is not consistent with the patient's 4-month history of symptoms.
